title: Images of smooth connected solvable normal subgroups under quotient homomorphisms
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G,H$ be affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:G\to H$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism, meaning that $F[G]$ is a faithfully flat module over $F[H]$ via $f^*$. Let $N\subseteq G$ be a smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Solvable means that iterating the derived subgroup eventually gives the trivial group scheme, where the derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism $(x,y)\mapsto xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ factors. Suppose $f|_N=j\circ q$ with $I$ an affine $F$-group scheme of finite type, $j:I\hookrightarrow H$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $q:N\to I$ a faithfully flat homomorphism, meaning that $F[N]$ is faithfully flat over $F[I]$. Then $I$ is smooth, connected and solvable, and $j$ identifies $I$ with a normal closed subgroup scheme of $H$. No finiteness or smoothness of $\ker f$ or $\ker q$ is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 5.39 and Remark 5.42, printed p.108 (image); Proposition 1.62(b), printed p.24 (smooth quotients); Proposition 6.27 and Proposition 6.30, printed pp.131--132 (solvable quotients and derived series); normality by conjugation and faithfully flat local lifting, as used in the proof of Lemma 19.14, printed p.400.

proof.text: Put $A=F[I]$ and $B=F[N]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] with the module $A$, the map $q^*:A\to B$ is injective. An injective map of $F$-vector spaces has an $F$-linear left inverse: extend a basis of its image to a basis of its target and project. Tensoring this left inverse with an identity, or with another left inverse, proves that tensor products of these injections over $F$ are injective. We use affine coordinates [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the identification $\operatorname{Spec}A'\times_F\operatorname{Spec}B'\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A'\otimes_FB')$ of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and the algebra tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]: the product of affine schemes has tensor coordinate ring, and maps to it are pairs of algebra maps. A map to $\operatorname{Spec}C$ factors through $\operatorname{Spec}(C/J)$ exactly when its pullback kills $J$, by [def-weil-closed-immersion] and the universal property of a quotient ring. Consequently an affine map with injective pullback detects both equality of morphisms to an affine target and factorization through a closed subscheme. Although the statement does not separately call $j$ a homomorphism, it is one: the two maps $I\times I\to H$ expressing preservation of multiplication agree after $q\times q$, whose pullback is injective; the identity follows by evaluating $f|_N=j q$ at $e_N$, and inverse compatibility follows after $q$.

source.place: Proposition 1.62(b), printed p.24: injectivity; Remark 5.40, printed p.108: detection through the quotient map. Coordinate details expanded here; Stacks Tag 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective).

proof.text: The following argument applies to any faithfully flat homomorphism $X\to Y$ of affine finite-type $F$-group schemes with $X$ smooth. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], every $X_L$ is reduced for every field extension $L/F$. The injection $F[Y]\hookrightarrow F[X]$ from step 1 remains injective after tensoring over $F$ with $L$, by its $F$-linear left inverse. If $a\in F[Y]\otimes_F L$ is nilpotent, its image in the reduced ring $F[X]\otimes_F L$ is zero, hence $a=0$. Thus $Y_L$ is reduced, using [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and $Y$ is geometrically reduced. Now [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth] applies to the finite-type group scheme $Y$ and gives smoothness. Apply this to $q:N\to I$ to obtain that $I$ is smooth.

source.place: Proposition 1.62(b), printed p.24, and Proposition 1.28, printed p.14; Stacks Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal) and Tags 047N, 047P.

proof.text: For any faithfully flat homomorphism $X\to Y$ as above, [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] makes the underlying map surjective. If $X$ is connected and $Y$ had a decomposition into two nonempty clopen subsets, their inverse images would be two nonempty clopen subsets partitioning $X$, contrary to [def-weil-connected-scheme]. The target is nonempty because it contains its identity. Thus connectedness also passes from $X$ to $Y$. In particular $I$ is connected. Neither this argument nor step 2 assumes that the kernel is smooth or finite.

source.place: Proposition 5.59(b), printed p.114, with the elementary topological argument; Stacks Tag 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings).

proof.text: Write $N_0=N$, $N_{r+1}=D(N_r)$. Repeated use of [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-derived-subgroup] shows that each $N_r$ is smooth connected affine of finite type and is the smallest closed subgroup containing the commutator morphism of $N_r$. The solvability hypothesis supplies an integer $t\geq0$ with $N_t=e$. For every $0\leq r\leq t$, apply [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] to $N_r\hookrightarrow N\xrightarrow{q}I$, giving $u_r:N_r\to J_r$ faithfully flat and $v_r:J_r\hookrightarrow I$ closed, with their composite equal to that map. Steps 2--3 also show that every $J_r$ is smooth connected. For $r=0$ take $J_0=I$, $u_0=q$, $v_0=1_I$. For $r=t$ take $J_t=e$ with its identity inclusion in $I$ and $u_t=1_e$; this inclusion is closed because on affine coordinates the counit $F[I]\to F$ is surjective. These choices include the case $t=0$.

source.place: Proposition 6.30 and the paragraph preceding it, printed p.132; Corollary 6.19(b), printed p.129; Theorem 5.39 and Remark 5.42, printed p.108.

proof.text: The commutator map $J_r\times J_r\to I$ (using $v_r$) factors through $J_{r+1}$. Indeed, pull it back along $u_r\times u_r$. For every algebra $R$ and $x,y\in N_r(R)$ its value becomes $q(xyx^{-1}y^{-1})$. The commutator of $N_r$ factors through $N_{r+1}$ by [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-derived-subgroup], and the composite $N_{r+1}\to I$ factors through $J_{r+1}$ by its chosen image factorization. Therefore the pullback of the ideal of $J_{r+1}$ vanishes after $u_r\times u_r$. This latter map has injective coordinate pullback by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] applied to $u_r$, and the tensor argument of step 1. The ideal already vanishes before pullback, proving the asserted factorization as a morphism of schemes, including on nonreduced test algebras.

source.place: Proposition 6.27 proof, printed p.131 (image of a solvable series), and Proposition 6.18, printed p.129 (commutator characterization); Stacks Tag 05CK.

proof.text: Inductively $D^r(I)\subseteq J_r$ for $0\leq r\leq t$. The base is $D^0(I)=I=J_0$. Suppose the inclusion holds at $r$. The commutator of $D^r(I)$, viewed in $I$, factors through $J_{r+1}$ by restriction of the factorization proved in step 5. Its image lies also in $D^r(I)$, so it factors through the intersection $D^r(I)\cap J_{r+1}$. This intersection is a closed subgroup: in affine coordinates it is the quotient by the sum of the two defining ideals, and on every test algebra its points are the intersection of the two subgroups. The smallest-closed-subgroup characterization of the derived subgroup in [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-derived-subgroup], applied within $D^r(I)$, gives $D^{r+1}(I)\subseteq D^r(I)\cap J_{r+1}\subseteq J_{r+1}$. That node applies successively because $I$ and all its derived subgroups are smooth connected affine of finite type. At $r=t$ we obtain $D^t(I)\subseteq J_t=e$, hence $D^t(I)=e$. This is solvability in the precise derived-series sense of the statement.

source.place: Proposition 6.30 proof, printed p.132, with the image-series argument of Proposition 6.27, printed p.131.

proof.text: It remains to prove normality in $H$. Put $C=F[H]$, $D=F[G]$ and let $K=\ker(j^*:C\to A)$ be the defining ideal of $I\subseteq H$. Let $c:H\times I\to H$ send $(h,i)$ to $h j(i)h^{-1}$. Its composite with $f\times q:G\times N\to H\times I$ sends $(g,n)$ to $f(gng^{-1})$. Normality of $N$ in $G$, in the pointwise sense of [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], means that conjugation $G\times N\to G$ factors through $N$: evaluate at the universal pair over $F[G]\otimes_F F[N]$ and use the affine quotient criterion of step 1. Thus this composite factors through $j:I\hookrightarrow H$, and $(f\times q)^*c^*(K)=0$. Both $f^*:C\to D$ and $q^*:A\to B$ are injective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective]. Their tensor product $C\otimes_F A\to D\otimes_F B$ is injective by step 1. Consequently $c^*(K)=0$, so $c$ itself factors through $I$. For every $F$-algebra $R$ this says $h j(I(R))h^{-1}\subseteq j(I(R))$; applying it to $h^{-1}$ gives equality. Hence $j(I(R))$ is normal for every $R$, exactly the required scheme-theoretic normality. Together with the given closed immersion and steps 2, 3 and 6 this proves every clause.

source.place: Lemma 19.14 proof, printed p.400 (normality because the ambient map is surjective), expanded by the affine ideal test; Stacks Tag 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective).
